researchQuestion: Could a historical backtest have known and used the selected filing value at the stated decision time?

executionPolicy.knowledgeClock: A filing fact becomes publicly available at its SEC acceptance timestamp, not at its fiscal period end.
executionPolicy.dailyTradabilityRule: For included CoreWeave cases, the conservative daily decision time is the next regular U.S. equity session open after SEC acceptance.
executionPolicy.versionSelectionRule: For each matched fact identity, select the latest source vintage with acceptedAt less than or equal to decisionTime.
executionPolicy.noSilentOverwrite: A later comparative, amended filing or AhaSignals correction creates a separately addressable version and never replaces a frozen predecessor.
executionPolicy.missingDataRule: Missing, ineligible or not-yet-public observations remain unavailable and are never converted to zero.

sourceDatasets.purpose: Fourteen matched CoreWeave facts with first-reported and later-comparative source vintages.
Preliminary six-issuer benchmark state before the Super Micro completed filing.
Filed six-issuer benchmark state and role-matched fiscal-period evidence.
Permanently archived source cross-section and citation anchor.

decisionCases.title: Later comparative value must not overwrite the first-reported value
decisionCases.question: Which CoreWeave Q2 2025 revenue value was knowable at the first tradable daily decision time after its August 2025 filing?
decisionCases.passRule: Select the latest source vintage whose SEC acceptance timestamp is on or before the decision time. The August 2026 comparative is excluded.

decisionCases.title: A later sign change must remain invisible to the earlier backtest
decisionCases.question: Does a 2025 decision retain the positive first-reported other-investing value instead of importing the negative 2026 comparative?
decisionCases.passRule: The earlier positive value remains active until the later filing is accepted; a sign flip in a later comparative cannot be backfilled.

decisionCases.title: Preliminary evidence must not be treated as a completed filing
decisionCases.question: Does the dataset preserve Super Micro as preliminary and outside the primary matrix before the completed Form 10-K?
decisionCases.passRule: Before the completed filing, retain the preliminary source status and exclusion from the primary filed-company matrix.

decisionCases.title: Unchanged values must still preserve evidence and tier changes
decisionCases.question: Can the pipeline distinguish an unchanged Super Micro revenue-growth value from the stronger evidence path that supports it later?
decisionCases.passRule: Report the evidence and comparability upgrade even when the derived numerical value remains unchanged.

decisionCases.title: Role-matched issuers must not be presented as a synchronized calendar-quarter rank
decisionCases.question: Does the pipeline keep different fiscal period ends visible before comparing NVIDIA and AMD?
decisionCases.passRule: Preserve both fiscal period ends and reject a synchronized calendar-quarter ranking when the dates differ.

performanceLayer.reason: The benchmark does not bundle market prices, corporate-action adjustments or return series. A compliant external price adapter is required before IC, turnover, return or drawdown differences can be calculated.

limitations: Version 1 tests data availability, source-vintage selection, evidence transitions and fiscal-period visibility. It does not test whether a feature earns an investment return.
The benchmark covers seven issuers and five known failure modes. Passing it does not establish that a pipeline is free from every form of look-ahead, survivorship or execution bias.
The daily tradability timestamps are explicit fixtures for the included filing dates, not a complete U.S. exchange calendar service.
SEC acceptance timestamps establish public availability; they do not establish when every market participant processed the filing.
Company names and symbols identify source filers only. AhaSignals is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by those issuers or the SEC.
The benchmark is research-only and is not investment, trading, legal, accounting or tax advice.
